chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Khadija Salim ibn Mukram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'The people are three: a scholar, a student, and scum (the worthless).'

key_terms.عَالِمٌ: scholar — one who possesses and practices religious knowledge; in the Shia tradition, this has special resonance with the role of the Imams as the supreme 'ulama'
key_terms.غُثَاءٌ: scum/froth/refuse — originally refers to the worthless debris carried on floodwaters; here used metaphorically for those who neither possess nor seek knowledge and thus have no spiritual worth
key_terms.مُتَعَلِّمٌ: student/learner — one who actively seeks knowledge; distinguished from the passive masses

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) classifies all of humanity into three groups: the scholar ('alim), the student (muta'allim), and the worthless (ghitha'). This tripartite division reflects a deeply Shia epistemological concern: knowledge ('ilm) is not merely an intellectual virtue but the defining characteristic of one's spiritual and moral status. The Imam implicitly calls his audience to refuse the third category by either becoming scholars or diligent students of the faith.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Ahmad Bin A’iz, from Abu Khadeeja Salim Bin Mukram, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The people are three (types) – a scholar<sup>asws</sup>, a student, and a scum (worthless)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Ahmad ibn ‘A’idh from abu Khadija Salim ibn Mukram from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
People are of three kinds: The scholars, the learning group and the garbled ones.”
